condition.purpose: Establish whether a Foreign National or qualifying ITIN borrower meets the foreign-national program requirements stated in the section.
steps: Determine whether the Foreign National or ITIN borrower meets the stated residence and authorization requirements.
Verify that the transaction is business purpose and concerns an investment property.
Apply the stated Foreign National CLTV limit for the transaction type and the stated FICO pricing requirement.
Check the escrow-waiver restriction and resolve the stated Credit Requirements restriction question.
Review the required post-close financial position and ability to mitigate exchange-rate fluctuations.
Review the referenced OFAC restrictions and state-specific exclusions.
checks: A Foreign National is a Non-Resident Alien not authorized to live or work in the U.S. and resides outside of the U.S.; an ITIN holder is eligible under this program only if the borrower resides outside of the U.S.
The transaction is business purpose and is an investment property.
For a Foreign National, CLTV is no more than 70% for purchase or 65% for refinance — rate & term and cash-out.
For a Foreign National, the loan is priced at FICO equal to 700.
A Foreign National is not receiving an escrow waiver.
Acra has confirmed the scope of the Credit Requirements panel’s statement “Foreign National ineligible”.
The applicant’s post-close financial position and ability to mitigate exchange rate fluctuations have been reviewed with scrutiny.
The applicable OFAC restrictions and state-specific exclusions have been reviewed.

condition.purpose: Establish whether the borrower has an eligible citizenship type and meets the requirements stated for that type.
steps: Check that the borrower’s citizenship type is one of the eligible types.
For a Permanent Resident, verify the required identification and Social Security documentation.
For a Non-Permanent Resident, verify proof of legal residency and resolve the stated limit interpretation.
For an ITIN borrower, check the stated loan amount, FICO, and CLTV limits, and resolve the stated eligibility and tier questions.
For an ITIN borrower, verify that scores and tradelines are reported under the correct ITIN or SSN.
checks: citizenship_type is one of: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN.
If citizenship_type is Permanent Resident, the borrower has an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89.
If citizenship_type is Non-Permanent Resident, the borrower has proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa.
If citizenship_type is Non-Permanent Resident, Acra has confirmed how to apply the printed limit “Max Loan Amount: $1.5M: Max CLTV 80%”.
If citizenship_type is ITIN, loan_amount is no more than $1.0M.
If citizenship_type is ITIN, FICO is at least 640.

If citizenship_type is ITIN, CLTV meets the printed tier for the applicable FICO and transaction: “FICO 700” is 70% purchase and 65% refinance — R/T and cash-out; “FICO 660 to 699” is 65% purchase and 60% refinance — R/T and cash-out; “FICO 640 to 659” is 60% purchase and 60% refinance — R/T and cash-out.
If citizenship_type is ITIN, Acra has confirmed whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above.
If citizenship_type is ITIN, scores and tradelines are reported under the correct ITIN or SSN to meet requirements.

outcomes.criterion: The citizenship type is eligible and every applicable citizenship-specific check holds, including resolution of the stated Acra confirmation questions.
The applicable requirements are met except that an Acra confirmation requested in this section remains outstanding.
The citizenship type is not eligible, or an applicable citizenship-specific check does not hold.
This job does not apply because the case has no borrower citizenship type to review.

condition.purpose: Calculate the DSCR for a file where a ratio is calculated.
steps: Identify annual in-place rent and market rent.
Use the lesser of those rent amounts as the numerator.
Determine the denominator from annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees; include subordinate financing if applicable.
Use the first payment due under the terms of the Note, then calculate the ratio.

The calculation uses the first payment due under the terms of the Note.

rule.description: Apply the stated DSCR formula without substituting other rent or payment measures.

ledger.clause:
STD-3.1 “Acra calculates the DSCR by dividing (a) the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent (reference §14.14) by (b) the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.2 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-26. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.3 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. Whether and when subordinate financing is permitted: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.4 §14.14 (market rent), referenced in the formula, is not reproduced in the excerpt (Appendix B). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

rule.description: Assess entity-borrower eligibility, ownership, guarantees, and required attestations against §6.1.

ledger.clause:
Section 3.12 governs loans to entities, the personal guarantees Acra requires, the entity documentation it accepts and title vesting in a revocable living trust. It is restated here as requirements; nothing in it is program-specific.

STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. See Q-09. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

rule.description: Verify the trust, its terms, and any required written exception for title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust under §6.4.

ledger.clause:
STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

condition.purpose: Determine whether foreign-account funds and funds held by Foreign Nationals meet the stated verification and closing requirements.
steps: For assets held in foreign accounts, verify U.S. Dollar equivalency using the current exchange rate via www.xe.com or the Wall Street Journal conversion table.
Verify that sufficient funds to close are on deposit with the Escrow / Closing Agent at least three (3) business days, including Saturdays for this calculation, prior to any closing date.
Obtain a copy of the two (2) most recent statements of the account. Translate bank statements in any language other than English into English.
If funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, obtain a letter of explanation and information comprising a sixty (60) day chain of funds.
For Foreign Nationals, verify a minimum of 60 days seasoning regardless of LTV / CLTV.

ledger.clause:
STD-5.6 Assets held / foreign accounts must be verified in U.S. Dollar equivalency at the current exchange rate via www.xe.com or the Wall Street Journal conversion table. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.7 Sufficient funds to close must be on deposit with the Escrow / Closing Agent at least three (3) business days (including Saturdays for this calculation) prior to any closing date. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.8 A copy of the two (2) most recent statements of that account is required. If the funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, a letter of explanation is required along with the information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds. Bank statements in any language other than English must be translated into English. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.9 Per §8.4, Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning, and funds held in a foreign bank / currency must be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing (STD-9.5). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether funds to close are documented for the required period and whether seasoning verification is required under the stated transaction and CLTV conditions.
steps: Require a minimum of 30-days documentation for all transactions.
Determine whether the seasoning-verification trigger applies: loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over $50,000 and over 70% CLTV.
Where source-account verification is required, review the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s).

For funds not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, review a letter of explanation and information comprising a sixty (60) day chain of funds where the applicable source-account requirements call for them.
Do not impose a domestic seasoning period beyond the stated 30-days documentation minimum absent the requested Acra confirmation.

For a business purpose loan, if funds to close are over $50,000 and CLTV is over 70%, seasoning of funds to close is verified.

Where funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days and the stated account-documentation condition applies, a letter of explanation and information comprising a sixty (60) day chain of funds are provided.

steps: Compare the loan amount with the stated minimum and maximum and check that it is in $50 increments.
Compare seller concessions and other contributions with the stated limit of 3% of the sale price.
For a transaction to which the applicant-contribution requirement applies, verify that the applicant contributes at least 10% of the purchase price in the applicant's own sourced and seasoned funds.
If gift funds are used, review the gift documentation required by the Seller's Guide gift-fund section; that section is not reproduced here.
checks: The loan amount is at least $100,000.
The loan amount is no more than $3,000,000.
The loan amount is in $50 increments.
Seller concessions / other contributions do not exceed 3% of the sale price.
The applicant's own sourced and seasoned funds contributed to the transaction are at least 10% of the purchase price when the applicant-contribution requirement applies.
When gift funds are used, the gift documentation meets the Seller's Guide gift-fund requirements.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable step is met and every check holds.
A requirement remains subject to conditions that must be cleared.
A step is not met or a check does not hold.
The job does not apply to this case.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the reserve requirements stated for applicable loan, borrower, and property circumstances are met.
steps: Determine whether LTV is > 80.00%; if so, verify 6 months PITIA reserves.
Determine whether FICO is < 620; if so, apply the stated 12 Months reserve requirement without assuming a payment basis not stated in the source.
For a first-time homebuyer, verify Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”).
For a vacant property, determine whether the transaction is a rate & term refinance or cash-out refinance and apply the corresponding stated minimum six months reserves or 6 months reserves.
If the property was listed for sale within six months, verify Twenty-four (24) months of reserves; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide.

For forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, where the subject is tenant-occupied and the prior two months' rent were not timely received, verify 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve; this may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.
If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, verify Two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.

Do not infer a base reserve requirement, a payment basis where only “months” is stated, permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, or whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional; Acra confirmation is requested in Q-07.
checks: If LTV is > 80.00%, 6 months PITIA reserves are held.
If FICO is < 620, the stated 12 Months reserve requirement is met; its payment basis is not specified in the source.
A first-time homebuyer has Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”).
For a vacant property — rate & term refinance, Minimum six months reserves are held.
For a vacant property — cash-out refinance, 6 months reserves are held.
If the property was listed for sale within six months, Twenty-four (24) months of reserves are held, with cash-in-hand considered only if otherwise consistent with the Guide.

If forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, and no timely receipt of the prior two months' rent all apply, 12 months of the subject's payment are held in reserve; the reserve may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.
If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, Two (2) months reserves are held for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.

condition.purpose: Determine the published maximum CLTV for the applicable Investment Property matrix entry and whether the case CLTV is within that value.
steps: Confirm whether the case is subject to the Investment Property matrix.
Select the transaction column corresponding to Purchase, Rate & Term, or Cash-Out.

For the selected tier and transaction column, select the row whose minimum-FICO threshold is the greatest threshold at or below fico; a score at or above a threshold and below the next higher threshold takes that row.
Read the cell at the selected row and column. Record NA where printed. For loans of $1,500,000 or less, record that there is no published matrix value below 600.
If the selected cell is a numeric percentage, compare cltv_pct with that percentage.
checks: The case’s loan amount, FICO, and transaction type identify one matrix tier, row, and column.
The selected matrix cell is a published numeric percentage, rather than NA or a case with no published matrix value.
If the selected matrix cell is a numeric percentage, cltv_pct does not exceed that percentage.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the case meets the additional loan-amount conditions and whether the stated matrix cash-in-hand footnote applies.
steps: If loan_amount is less than $200,000, apply the maximum CLTV of 80% for Purchase or 75% for refinance (Rate & Term and Cash-Out).
If loan_amount is greater than $2,000,000, verify that DSCR is 1.0 or greater.
If the loan is interest-only, verify the minimum loan amount of $250,000, maximum loan amount of $3,000,000, and minimum FICO of 640.
If delayed financing applies, apply the stated $1.5MM cap.
For Cash-Out, where LTV is greater than 65%, apply footnote 1: maximum cash-in-hand is $1,000,000 for loans ≥ $1,500,000 and $500,000 for loans < $1,500,000.

Note footnote 2 as printed: “When LTV ≤ 65%, unlimited cash-in-hand allowed”. The source requests Acra confirmation on whether footnote 2 applies to every tier or only the tier bearing its marker, and why the footnotes use LTV while the matrix is labelled CLTV.
checks: If loan_amount is less than $200,000 and loan_purpose is Purchase, cltv_pct is no more than 80%.
If loan_amount is less than $200,000 and loan_purpose is Rate & Term or Cash-Out, cltv_pct is no more than 75%.
If loan_amount is greater than $2,000,000, DSCR is at least 1.0.
If the loan is interest-only, loan_amount is at least $250,000.
If the loan is interest-only, loan_amount is no more than $3,000,000.
If the loan is interest-only, fico is at least 640.
If delayed financing applies, loan_amount is no more than $1.5MM.
If the loan is Cash-Out and LTV is greater than 65%, cash-in-hand is no more than the applicable footnote 1 cap.
The applicable treatment of footnote 2 and the LTV-versus-CLTV footnotes is confirmed where needed.

PLAT-1.7 The program is offered through two channels with different minimum ratios: Correspondent ≥ 1.2, Wholesale ≥ 1.0 (PLAT-3.7). Matrix footnote 3 also restricts Correspondent pricing (PLAT-2.3). \[P: Minimum DSCR; matrix footnote 3\]

PLAT-1.8 Every loan must meet the applicable channel minimum DSCR. The Platinum Summary lists no No Ratio option and no allowance for a ratio below 1.0; a ratio below the channel minimum does not meet the published requirement. Whether No Ratio or sub-1.0 qualification exists on this program in any form: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-1.9 Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. The Standard Summary's statement that borrowing-entity income documentation is not required does not appear in the Platinum Summary; whether it applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. \[G §7.3, p. 5\]

PLAT-1.10 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions”; the Platinum Summary refers to market rent “as established on the 1007 or 1025”. Whether a Form 1025 alone satisfies the requirement for a two-unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-04. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4; P: Income Documentation\]

PLAT-1.11 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (PLAT-7.9 to 7.12). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

PLAT-1.12 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

The Platinum Summary states its own rule for qualifying rent; the Seller's Guide excerpt supplies the denominator, the payment used, the rent-schedule requirements and the treatment of applicants with recent forbearance or lates. Both are quoted where they differ.

PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-3.4 Denominator, per §5.32: “the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.5 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.6 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. The Platinum Summary does not address subordinate financing or restate the Standard Summary's HELOC calculation: Acra confirmation requested → Q-15. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.7 Minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio: Correspondent ≥ 1.2; Wholesale ≥ 1.0. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-3.8 Property listed for sale within six months (§11.5): the excerpt requires “≥1.0 DSCR”; on this program the channel minimum applies — Wholesale 1.0, Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-7.8). \[G §11.5, p. 11; P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-9.3 “Interest-Only (5 Yr Term), Max CLTV: 75.00%”. \[P: Product Requirements — Restrictions\]

PLAT-9.4 No minimum loan amount or minimum FICO is printed for interest-only loans on Platinum Select: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09. \[P: Product Requirements\]

PLAT-9.5 Interest-only is not available on a property listed for sale (PLAT-7.8). \[G §11.5, p. 11\]

PLAT-9.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (PLAT-3.5; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-21). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the entity documentation required by PLAT-5.10 is complete and acceptable for review under the stated requirements.
steps: Obtain a complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments.

For LLCs and Partnerships, obtain a complete, legible Operating Agreement with all referenced exhibits and all amendments; for corporations, obtain the Bylaws with all referenced exhibits and all amendments. Verify that the document states whether the entity is member or manager managed, authorizes borrowing money and entering into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Determine whether additional information is required if formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

Obtain documentation evidencing all ownership interests. For LLCs and Partnerships, verify that the Operating Agreement identifies by name all persons and their ownership interest or attaches that information as an exhibit, or that membership interest certificates / units are provided in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

For S or C Corporations, obtain shareholder / stockholder certificates complying with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation’s stock ledger. Verify that the certificate or ledger accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, obtain an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate.

For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, obtain the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest; if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed, verify that the letter includes a statement to that effect.
Verify that names on entity documents match the identification; if they do not match exactly, obtain a letter of explanation addressing the discrepancy.
Obtain a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is conducted or the property is located, obtain a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted.

Obtain the entity’s IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter. If an EIN exception is requested, verify that it is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

Obtain a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. Check whether the Operating Agreement or Bylaws require it even where ownership is held by one individual. Do not accept it to designate a signor on a personal guarantee.
If an attorney in fact is designated to execute a personal guarantee, verify that the principal utilizes a Power of Attorney for that designation.
Record any additional supporting documentation Legal conditions for in its sole discretion.

rule.description: Review the required entity documents and verify that each specified document and content requirement is satisfied.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

ledger.clause:
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

Section 3.12 governs loans to entities, the personal guarantees Acra requires, the entity documentation it accepts and title vesting in a revocable living trust. Nothing in the Platinum Summary modifies it; whether it applies to Platinum Select unchanged is Q-13.

PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Assess the reserve requirements stated for CLTV, property listed for sale, recent forbearance or mortgage lates with tenant occupancy, and unavailable rent loss insurance.
steps: If CLTV is greater than 75.00%, check for 6-months Reserves required for CLTV > 75.00%.
If the property was listed for sale within six months, check for twenty-four (24) months of reserves. Cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide.

Determine whether the property is tenant-occupied and whether there was forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months without timely receipt of the prior two months' rent. If so, check for 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve; this may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand. The relationship to 0x30x12 is unresolved in the source.
If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, check for two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.

Do not assume a base reserve requirement at CLTV of 75.00% or below, a payment basis, permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, or whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional; obtain Acra confirmation.
checks: If cltv_pct > 75.00%, reserves_months >= 6.
If listed_for_sale_last_6_months is true, reserves_months >= 24.

If there was forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, the subject is tenant-occupied, and the prior two months' rent was not received timely, 12 months of the subject's payment are held in reserve.
If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, reserves equal two (2) months for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.

The base reserve requirement at CLTV of 75.00% or below, payment basis, permitted sources, cumulative treatment of overlapping triggers, and treatment of reserves substituted for rent loss insurance as additional reserves have been confirmed by Acra where applicable.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable reserve trigger is identified, each corresponding reserve check holds, and all applicable unresolved reserve terms have been confirmed by Acra.
No applicable reserve check is known to fail, but trigger facts, reserve amounts, or applicable Acra confirmations remain outstanding.
Any applicable reserve check does not hold.
No stated reserve trigger applies and no unresolved base reserve requirement applies to the case.

condition.purpose: Determine whether CLTV meets the matrix and the additional stated limits and adjustments.
steps: Apply the matrix row for the decisioning score and loan purpose: 730 and above, 80% for Purchase, 80% for Rate & Term, and 75% for Cash-Out; 721 through 729, 80%, 80%, and 65%, respectively; 700 through 720 on a literal reading of the printed thresholds, 80%, 80%, and 55%, respectively.
Apply the 75.00% maximum CLTV when the loan amount is less than $350,000 or greater than $1,500,000.
Apply the 75.00% maximum CLTV for a Warrantable Condo or Two-Units property.
Apply the 75.00% maximum CLTV for Interest-Only (5 Yr Term).
Apply the 65% LTV / CLTV maximum when the property was listed for sale within six months.
For Correspondent loans with a score of 700-719, apply the stated 60% CLTV restriction; for a cash-out loan in that score range, do not use that restriction to raise the matrix’s 55% limit.
For a declining-market property, account for the stated -5% CLTV adjustment and obtain confirmation of how it combines with other caps.
Where the score is 720, or the Correspondent 700-719 restriction interacts with the matrix by purpose, obtain the requested Acra confirmation on treatment of the printed 721 threshold and the limits.
checks: cltv_pct does not exceed the matrix maximum for the decisioning score and loan_purpose, using the printed thresholds literally.
If loan_amount is less than $350,000 or greater than $1,500,000, cltv_pct does not exceed 75.00%.
If property_type is Warrantable Condo or Two-Units, cltv_pct does not exceed 75.00%.
If product_is_interest_only is true, cltv_pct does not exceed 75.00%.
If listed_for_sale_last_6_months is true, cltv_pct does not exceed 65%.
If channel is Correspondent and the decisioning score is from 700 through 719, cltv_pct does not exceed 60%; a cash-out case in this range must also meet the matrix maximum.
If the property is in a declining market, the -5% CLTV adjustment is applied using the combination with other caps confirmed by Acra.
If the case has a score of 720, or is a Correspondent case with a score of 700-719, the applicable Q-01 treatment has been confirmed by Acra.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable CLTV check holds, and any applicable Q-01 or Q-08 treatment has been confirmed and applied.
A Q-01 or Q-08 confirmation or declining-market profile needed to determine the applicable CLTV limit is pending.
Any applicable CLTV check does not hold.
The case has no CLTV limit to assess.

missing_reads: Confirmation under Q-01 of whether the printed 721 threshold is intended and how a score of 720 is treated, including how the Correspondent restriction applies by purpose; whether the property is in a declining market and the property/borrower full profile needed for the -5% CLTV adjustment; confirmation under Q-08 of how that reduction combines with other caps.

rule.description: Identify each applicable published CLTV cap and check the case CLTV against it.

ledger.clause:
One matrix covers all loan amounts to \$2,000,000. It is reproduced below exactly as printed, followed by its footnotes in Acra's words. The printed FICO thresholds are 730, 721 and 700, which leaves a score of exactly 720 to be read literally; the reading and its consequences are set out for Acra to confirm rather than adopted. PLAT-2.1 The rows below are Acra's. Each row is a minimum-FICO threshold: a score at or above the threshold and below the next higher threshold takes that row. No row is printed below 700. \[P: Loan Amount, FICO, CLTV Requirements\] | **Min FICO** | **Purchase** | **Rate & Term** | **Cash-Out** | |--------------|--------------|-----------------|--------------| | 730 | 80% | 80% | 75% | | 721 | 80% | 80% | 65% | | 700 | 80% | 80% | 55% |

THE PRINTED 721 THRESHOLD AND A SCORE OF 720

Read literally, a decisioning score of 720 falls in the 700 row (cash-out maximum 55%), sits outside the Correspondent restriction printed for “700-719 FICO” (footnote 3), and takes the 3.25 ARM margin printed for “720-759”. This document does not normalize 721 to 720. Whether the 721 threshold is intended, and how 720 is treated on each of the three points: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.
PLAT-2.2 Footnote 1, whose marker is printed on the Cash-Out column heading: “When LTV \> 65% Max Cash-in-Hand: \$1,000,000 for loans ≥ \$1,500,000, \$500,000 for loans \< \$1,500,000.” Footnote 2, whose marker appears nowhere in the matrix: “When LTV ≤ 65%, unlimited cash-in-hand allowed.” The footnotes are stated in LTV while the matrix is labelled CLTV: Acra confirmation requested → Q-16. \[P: matrix footnotes 1–2\] PLAT-2.3 Footnote 3, whose marker also appears nowhere in the matrix: “Correspondent Pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 FICO”. For a Correspondent cash-out at 700-719 the matrix already prints 55%; the 60% footnote does not raise that figure. How the two limits apply together by purpose: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01. \[P: matrix footnote 3\] PLAT-2.4 Footnote \*: “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM” (PLAT-1.4, Q-02). \[P: matrix footnote\] PLAT-2.5 Loan amount \< \$350,000 or \> \$1,500,000: maximum CLTV 75.00% (PLAT-1.14). \[P: Loan Amount Requirements\] PLAT-1.16 Under the heading “Ineligible State: Non-Owner Occupied” the Summary lists “SD, U.S. Terrs.” \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\] PLAT-1.17 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile”. How this reduction combines with other caps: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\] PLAT-7.1 Eligible property types: SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Two-Units. “Two-Units, Warrantable Condo, Max CLTV: 75.00%”. \[P: Subject Property Requirements\] PLAT-7.2 “Rural Properties, Condotels, Non-Warrantable Condos ineligible”; “Short-Term Rentals (STR) ineligible”. \[P: Subject Property Requirements\] | **Feature** | **Status in the Platinum Summary** | **Where stated** | |----|----|----| | SFR, Townhome, PUD | Expressly eligible | PLAT-7.1 | | Warrantable Condo | Expressly eligible; maximum CLTV 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 | | Two-Units | Expressly eligible; maximum CLTV 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 | | Rural Properties | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 | | Condotels | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 | | Non-Warrantable Condos | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 | | Short-Term Rentals | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 | | Three- and four-unit properties | Not addressed — Q-07 | — | | Manufactured homes | Not addressed — Q-07 | — | | Mixed use; Adult Care / Assisted Living (§10.7) | Not addressed — Q-07 | — | | PUDtel | Not addressed — Q-07 | — | PLAT-7.3 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile” (PLAT-1.17). \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\] PLAT-7.4 Ineligible locations: SD, U.S. Terrs. (PLAT-1.16). \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\] PLAT-9.3 “Interest-Only (5 Yr Term), Max CLTV: 75.00%”. \[P: Product Requirements — Restrictions\] PLAT-9.4 No minimum loan amount or minimum FICO is printed for interest-only loans on Platinum Select: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09. \[P: Product Requirements\] PLAT-9.5 Interest-only is not available on a property listed for sale (PLAT-7.8). \[G §11.5, p. 11\] PLAT-9.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (PLAT-3.5; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-21). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\] | **Condition** | **Purchase** | **Rate & Term** | **Cash-Out** | **Stated at** | |----|----|----|----|----| | Matrix, FICO 730 and above | 80% | 80% | 75% | PLAT-2.1 | | Matrix, FICO 721–729 | 80% | 80% | 65% | PLAT-2.1 | | Matrix, FICO 700–720 (literal reading, Q-01) | 80% | 80% | 55% | PLAT-2.1 | | Correspondent, “700-719 FICO” | 60% | 60% | 60% (matrix prints 55%) | PLAT-2.3 | | Loan amount \< \$350,000 | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-1.14 | | Loan amount \> \$1,500,000 | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-1.14 | | Warrantable Condo | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 | | Two-Units | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 | | Interest-Only (5 Yr Term) | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-9.3 | | Listed for sale within six months (LTV / CLTV) | 65% | 65% | 65% | PLAT-7.8 | | Declining market (adjustment) | −5% | −5% | −5% | PLAT-1.17 |

PLAT-1.7 The program is offered through two channels with different minimum ratios: Correspondent ≥ 1.2, Wholesale ≥ 1.0 (PLAT-3.7). Matrix footnote 3 also restricts Correspondent pricing (PLAT-2.3). \[P: Minimum DSCR; matrix footnote 3\]

PLAT-1.8 Every loan must meet the applicable channel minimum DSCR. The Platinum Summary lists no No Ratio option and no allowance for a ratio below 1.0; a ratio below the channel minimum does not meet the published requirement. Whether No Ratio or sub-1.0 qualification exists on this program in any form: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-1.9 Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. The Standard Summary's statement that borrowing-entity income documentation is not required does not appear in the Platinum Summary; whether it applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. \[G §7.3, p. 5\]

PLAT-1.10 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions”; the Platinum Summary refers to market rent “as established on the 1007 or 1025”. Whether a Form 1025 alone satisfies the requirement for a two-unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-04. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4; P: Income Documentation\]

PLAT-1.11 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (PLAT-7.9 to 7.12). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

PLAT-1.12 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Apply the foreign-national program’s eligibility rules, limits, and restrictions.
PURPOSE: Establish whether a Foreign National or qualifying ITIN borrower meets the foreign-national program requirements stated in the section.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - The transaction is business purpose and is an investment property.
  - For a Foreign National, CLTV is no more than 70% for purchase or 65% for refinance — rate & term and cash-out.
  - A Foreign National is not receiving an escrow waiver.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - A Foreign National is a Non-Resident Alien not authorized to live or work in the U.S. and resides outside of the U.S.; an ITIN holder is eligible under this program only if the borrower resides outside of the U.S.
  - For a Foreign National, the loan is priced at FICO equal to 700.
  - Acra has confirmed the scope of the Credit Requirements panel’s statement “Foreign National ineligible”.
  - The applicant’s post-close financial position and ability to mitigate exchange rate fluctuations have been reviewed with scrutiny.
  - The applicable OFAC restrictions and state-specific exclusions have been reviewed.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-4.7 Foreign National ineligible for the escrow waiver (STD-7.12). \[S: Escrow Waiver\]

STD-4.8 The Credit Requirements panel also states “Foreign National ineligible” under Restrictions, without stating its scope: Acra confirmation requested → Q-04. \[S: Credit Requirements\]

Section 3.10 of the Seller's Guide, reproduced in the excerpt, governs foreign nationals on business-purpose transactions. Its OFAC restrictions and state-specific exclusions are referred to but not reproduced.

STD-5.1 Foreign Nationals are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions only (i.e. investment properties). \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.2 Eligible under the Foreign National Program are Non-Resident Aliens who are not authorized to live or work in the U.S. “A true Foreign National may periodically visit the U.S. for various reasons including vacation and / or business, may purchase property for limited personal use or investment, or may own a U.S based business entity, but they must reside outside of the U.S.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.3 Borrowers who are holders of Individual Tax Identification Numbers (ITIN) are eligible for this program if they reside outside of the U.S. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.4 “Due to market exchange rates, applicants are to be reviewed with scrutiny toward a post-close financial position and their ability to mitigate exchange rate fluctuations.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.5 “See 3.10 for OFAC restrictions and state specific exclusions” — not reproduced (Appendix B). \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

proposals.reasoning: The source permits Foreign National financing only on business-purpose transactions, identified there as investment properties. The encoded Foreign National limits are CLTV no more than 70 for purchase and 65 for refinance, and no escrow waiver. Those numbers remain as printed because cltv_pct is in percent units. The source does not state these CLTV and escrow restrictions for ITIN borrowers, so they are not applied to them. Residence, authorization, FICO, reviewer scrutiny, OFAC/state exclusions, and the unresolved Credit Requirements panel statement are not evaluated.

  - If citizenship_type is ITIN, CLTV meets the printed tier for the applicable FICO and transaction: “FICO 700” is 70% purchase and 65% refinance — R/T and cash-out; “FICO 660 to 699” is 65% purchase and 60% refinance — R/T and cash-out; “FICO 640 to 659” is 60% purchase and 60% refinance — R/T and cash-out.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - If citizenship_type is Permanent Resident, the borrower has an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89.
  - If citizenship_type is Non-Permanent Resident, the borrower has proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa.
  - If citizenship_type is Non-Permanent Resident, Acra has confirmed how to apply the printed limit “Max Loan Amount: $1.5M: Max CLTV 80%”.
  - If citizenship_type is ITIN, Acra has confirmed whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above.
  - If citizenship_type is ITIN, scores and tradelines are reported under the correct ITIN or SSN to meet requirements.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
Eligible citizenship types and their limits come from the Summary. The foreign-national program and borrowing entities come from the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in sections 5 and 6; first-time homebuyers are in 4.3.

STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. Limit printed as “Max Loan Amount: \$1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” — whether this is two independent limits or one conditional limit: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.4 Foreign National: “Borrowers whose Primary Residence is not located in the United States of America.” Maximum CLTV 70% (purchase) and 65% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out); “Price loan at FICO equal to 700”. No maximum loan amount is stated for foreign nationals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. Program documentation is in section 5. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.5 ITIN: “ITIN is defined as any non-resident that is unable to provide any of the ‘Non-Permanent Resident Alien’ documents listed above.” Maximum loan amount \$1.0M; minimum FICO 640; maximum CLTV by FICO as printed below. §3.10 separately admits ITIN holders under the foreign-national program when they reside outside the US. Whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible, and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[S: Borrower Citizenship; G §3.10, p. 6\]

| **ITIN tier as printed** | **Purchase** | **Refinance — R/T and cash-out** |
|--------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| “FICO 700”               | 70%          | 65%                              |
| “FICO 660 to 699”        | 65%          | 60%                              |
| “FICO 640 to 659”        | 60%          | 60%                              |

STD-4.6 “Scores & tradelines must be reported under the correct ITIN or SSN to meet requirements.” \[S: Credit Requirements\]

proposals.reasoning: Corrected the ITIN CLTV limits to use percentage-point values because cltv_pct is expressed as a percent (for example, 60 means 60%). Preserved the stated citizenship checks, ITIN amount and minimum-FICO limits, tier boundaries, and handling of scores above the printed FICO 700 tier.

STD-1.10 Minimum loan amount \$100,000; maximum loan amount \$3,000,000; loan amount to be in \$50 increments. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.11 Seller concession / other contributions: limited to 3% of the sale price. \[S: Loan Amount\]

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Identify each stated reserve trigger and verify its printed reserve requirement without supplying unstated bases or cumulative rules.
PURPOSE: Determine whether the reserve requirements stated for applicable loan, borrower, and property circumstances are met.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:

  - A first-time homebuyer has Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”).
  - If the property was listed for sale within six months, Twenty-four (24) months of reserves are held, with cash-in-hand considered only if otherwise consistent with the Guide.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - If LTV is > 80.00%, 6 months PITIA reserves are held.
  - For a vacant property — rate & term refinance, Minimum six months reserves are held.
  - For a vacant property — cash-out refinance, 6 months reserves are held.
  - If forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, and no timely receipt of the prior two months' rent all apply, 12 months of the subject's payment are held in reserve; the reserve may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.
  - If rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, Two (2) months reserves are held for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-9.6 The sources state reserves only for the situations below, and state the payment basis only where shown. | **Trigger** | **Reserves as printed** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| LTV \> 80.00% | 6 months PITIA reserves | S: Income Documentation |
| FICO \< 620 | 12 Months | S: Credit Requirements |
| First-time homebuyer | Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”) | G §3.13; S: Restrictions |
| Vacant property — rate & term refinance | Minimum six months reserves | G §10.17; S: Occupancy Type |
| Vacant property — cash-out refinance | 6 months reserves | S: Occupancy Type |
| Property listed for sale within six months | Twenty-four (24) months of reserves; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide | G §11.5 |
| Forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, without timely receipt of the prior two months' rent | 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve, which may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand | G §5.32 |
| Rent loss insurance required but cannot be obtained | Two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided | G §23.40 |

proposals.reasoning: Checks only the three designated triggers against the printed reserve amounts: FICO below 620 requires 12 months, first-time homebuyer requires at least six months, and a property listed for sale within six months requires 24 months. No payment basis is inferred for the FICO requirement, and reviewer-only checks are not encoded.

condition.source:
import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    loan_amount = ctx['loan_amount']
    fico = ctx['fico']
    loan_purpose = ctx['loan_purpose']
    cltv_pct = ctx['cltv_pct']

    missing = rules_lib.gaps(
        loan_amount=loan_amount,
        fico=fico,
        loan_purpose=loan_purpose,
        cltv_pct=cltv_pct,
    )
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    # STD-2.2 states that loans of $1,500,000 or less have no published
    # matrix row below FICO 600.
    if loan_amount <= 1500000 and fico < 600:
        return False

    # The clause supplies no loan-amount boundaries or labels for its three
    # tables, so the applicable tier and matrix cell cannot be determined.
    return rules_lib.unknown('published loan-amount tier')

condition.source:
import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    cltv_pct = ctx['cltv_pct']
    occupancy_subtype = ctx['occupancy_subtype']
    residential_unit_count = ctx['residential_unit_count']

    missing = rules_lib.gaps(
        cltv_pct=cltv_pct,
        occupancy_subtype=occupancy_subtype,
        residential_unit_count=residential_unit_count,
    )
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    units_in_range = rules_lib.match(residential_unit_count, (1, 2, 3, 4)) is not None
    non_owner_income_property = rules_lib.match(
        occupancy_subtype,
        (
            'Investment',
            'Investment Property',
            'Non-Owner Occupied',
            'Non-Owner Occupied Investment Property',
            'Non-Owner Occupied Income Property',
            'Rental',
            'Rental Property',
        ),
    ) is not None

    return units_in_range and non_owner_income_property and cltv_pct > 70

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-platinum.entity_guarantor_and_trust_requirements.entity_eligibility_and_guarantees

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify the entity, ownership structure, required guarantors, and related eligibility conditions against the stated requirements.
PURPOSE: Determine whether an entity borrower and its ownership and guarantee arrangements meet PLAT-5.1 through PLAT-5.9.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - The transaction is a business purpose transaction involving an investment property exclusively.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - Collateral title is held directly by individual person(s) or by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion.
  - Every individual with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provides an Acra-approved recourse guarantee or Exhibit 7.
  - Where there are multiple guarantors, all recourse is joint and several.
  - The entity borrower is a single purpose entity as defined in PLAT-5.4 and is not a series limited liability company.
  - Every entity that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and be on title as a direct owner is a borrowing entity.
  - No ownership-percentage change with intent to circumvent required personal guarantors is recognized, and no such change is made within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process.
  - The entity is US formed and based, is not foreign owned, and is of an allowed type rather than a prohibited type.
  - The entity ownership structure complies with the stated one-subsidiary limit and does not involve multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera.
  - At least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience.
  - At least one borrower / guarantor attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

Section 3.12 governs loans to entities, the personal guarantees Acra requires, the entity documentation it accepts and title vesting in a revocable living trust. Nothing in the Platinum Summary modifies it; whether it applies to Platinum Select unchanged is Q-13.

PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

proposals.reasoning: Encodes only the PLAT-5.1 requirement that the transaction be for a business purpose and involve an investment property exclusively. Other entity, ownership, guarantee, and eligibility checks are left to the reviewer. Missing or uninterpretable required values are returned as cannot tell.
