CHECKS TO ENCODE: - cltv_pct does not exceed the matrix maximum for the decisioning score and loan_purpose, using the printed thresholds literally. - If loan_amount is less than $350,000 or greater than $1,500,000, cltv_pct does not exceed 75.00%. - If property_type is Warrantable Condo or Two-Units, cltv_pct does not exceed 75.00%. - If product_is_interest_only is true, cltv_pct does not exceed 75.00%. - If listed_for_sale_last_6_months is true, cltv_pct does not exceed 65%. - If channel is Correspondent and the decisioning score is from 700 through 719, cltv_pct does not exceed 60%; a cash-out case in this range must also meet the matrix maximum. CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER: - If the property is in a declining market, the -5% CLTV adjustment is applied using the combination with other caps confirmed by Acra. - If the case has a score of 720, or is a Correspondent case with a score of 700-719, the applicable Q-01 treatment has been confirmed by Acra. SOURCE CLAUSE: One matrix covers all loan amounts to \$2,000,000. It is reproduced below exactly as printed, followed by its footnotes in Acra's words. The printed FICO thresholds are 730, 721 and 700, which leaves a score of exactly 720 to be read literally; the reading and its consequences are set out for Acra to confirm rather than adopted. PLAT-2.1 The rows below are Acra's. Each row is a minimum-FICO threshold: a score at or above the threshold and below the next higher threshold takes that row. No row is printed below 700. \[P: Loan Amount, FICO, CLTV Requirements\] | **Min FICO** | **Purchase** | **Rate & Term** | **Cash-Out** | |--------------|--------------|-----------------|--------------| | 730 | 80% | 80% | 75% | | 721 | 80% | 80% | 65% | | 700 | 80% | 80% | 55% |

THE PRINTED 721 THRESHOLD AND A SCORE OF 720

Read literally, a decisioning score of 720 falls in the 700 row (cash-out maximum 55%), sits outside the Correspondent restriction printed for “700-719 FICO” (footnote 3), and takes the 3.25 ARM margin printed for “720-759”. This document does not normalize 721 to 720. Whether the 721 threshold is intended, and how 720 is treated on each of the three points: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.
PLAT-2.2 Footnote 1, whose marker is printed on the Cash-Out column heading: “When LTV \> 65% Max Cash-in-Hand: \$1,000,000 for loans ≥ \$1,500,000, \$500,000 for loans \< \$1,500,000.” Footnote 2, whose marker appears nowhere in the matrix: “When LTV ≤ 65%, unlimited cash-in-hand allowed.” The footnotes are stated in LTV while the matrix is labelled CLTV: Acra confirmation requested → Q-16. \[P: matrix footnotes 1–2\] PLAT-2.3 Footnote 3, whose marker also appears nowhere in the matrix: “Correspondent Pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 FICO”. For a Correspondent cash-out at 700-719 the matrix already prints 55%; the 60% footnote does not raise that figure. How the two limits apply together by purpose: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01. \[P: matrix footnote 3\] PLAT-2.4 Footnote \*: “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM” (PLAT-1.4, Q-02). \[P: matrix footnote\] PLAT-2.5 Loan amount \< \$350,000 or \> \$1,500,000: maximum CLTV 75.00% (PLAT-1.14). \[P: Loan Amount Requirements\] PLAT-1.16 Under the heading “Ineligible State: Non-Owner Occupied” the Summary lists “SD, U.S. Terrs.” \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\] PLAT-1.17 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile”. How this reduction combines with other caps: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\] PLAT-7.1 Eligible property types: SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Two-Units. “Two-Units, Warrantable Condo, Max CLTV: 75.00%”. \[P: Subject Property Requirements\] PLAT-7.2 “Rural Properties, Condotels, Non-Warrantable Condos ineligible”; “Short-Term Rentals (STR) ineligible”. \[P: Subject Property Requirements\] | **Feature** | **Status in the Platinum Summary** | **Where stated** | |----|----|----| | SFR, Townhome, PUD | Expressly eligible | PLAT-7.1 | | Warrantable Condo | Expressly eligible; maximum CLTV 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 | | Two-Units | Expressly eligible; maximum CLTV 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 | | Rural Properties | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 | | Condotels | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 | | Non-Warrantable Condos | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 | | Short-Term Rentals | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 | | Three- and four-unit properties | Not addressed — Q-07 | — | | Manufactured homes | Not addressed — Q-07 | — | | Mixed use; Adult Care / Assisted Living (§10.7) | Not addressed — Q-07 | — | | PUDtel | Not addressed — Q-07 | — | PLAT-7.3 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile” (PLAT-1.17). \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\] PLAT-7.4 Ineligible locations: SD, U.S. Terrs. (PLAT-1.16). \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\] PLAT-9.3 “Interest-Only (5 Yr Term), Max CLTV: 75.00%”. \[P: Product Requirements — Restrictions\] PLAT-9.4 No minimum loan amount or minimum FICO is printed for interest-only loans on Platinum Select: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09. \[P: Product Requirements\] PLAT-9.5 Interest-only is not available on a property listed for sale (PLAT-7.8). \[G §11.5, p. 11\] PLAT-9.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (PLAT-3.5; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-21). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\] | **Condition** | **Purchase** | **Rate & Term** | **Cash-Out** | **Stated at** | |----|----|----|----|----| | Matrix, FICO 730 and above | 80% | 80% | 75% | PLAT-2.1 | | Matrix, FICO 721–729 | 80% | 80% | 65% | PLAT-2.1 | | Matrix, FICO 700–720 (literal reading, Q-01) | 80% | 80% | 55% | PLAT-2.1 | | Correspondent, “700-719 FICO” | 60% | 60% | 60% (matrix prints 55%) | PLAT-2.3 | | Loan amount \< \$350,000 | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-1.14 | | Loan amount \> \$1,500,000 | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-1.14 | | Warrantable Condo | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 | | Two-Units | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 | | Interest-Only (5 Yr Term) | 75.00% | 75.00% | 75.00% | PLAT-9.3 | | Listed for sale within six months (LTV / CLTV) | 65% | 65% | 65% | PLAT-7.8 | | Declining market (adjustment) | −5% | −5% | −5% | PLAT-1.17 |

proposals.reasoning: The function applies the printed matrix rows literally, including assigning a score of 720 to the 700 row, then enforces each stated additional cap by taking the lowest applicable maximum. Percentages are compared as the printed numeric percent values because cltv_pct is in percent units. It does not apply the declining-market adjustment or make any other reviewer-only determination. Scores below 700 have no printed matrix row, so the matrix result is returned as undecidable rather than inventing a cap.

SKILL: Apply the stated decisioning-score selection rule, minimum score, and tradeline requirements.
PURPOSE: Determine whether the decisioning score and tradelines meet PLAT-6.1 through PLAT-6.5.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - fico is at least 700.
  - credit_score_count is 3, or credit_score_count is 2 or fewer and tradelines_meet_requirement is true.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - The decisioning score is selected in accordance with PLAT-6.1.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
PLAT-6.1 “Decisioning Credit Score: Primary Wage Earner middle score. For loans that close in the name of an entity, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors, presuming equal percentages of ownership. If ownership percentages differ, use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.2 Minimum decisioning score 700 (no matrix row below 700, PLAT-2.1); Correspondent pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 (PLAT-2.3). \[P: matrix; footnote 3\]

PLAT-6.3 “Tradelines: Applicants with scores from 3 repositories are deemed to be acceptable with no tradeline overlay. 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history for applicants with 2 or fewer scores.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.4 Applicants with one score are within “2 or fewer scores” for the tradeline requirement above. The Platinum Summary does not state how the decisioning score is set with one score or with two scores, whether any no-score pathway exists, or how “Primary Wage Earner” is identified on a file with no income documentation. The Standard Summary's one-or-no-score provision is not restated here: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.5 Where two or more guarantors hold an equal largest ownership interest and ownership is not equal across all guarantors, PLAT-6.1 does not say whose score is used: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

proposals.reasoning: Applies the stated 700 minimum and the stated repository-count/tradeline rule. For three scores, the source says there is no tradeline overlay, so the tradeline field is not read. The decisioning-score selection rule is left to a reviewer and does not affect this result.

SOURCE CLAUSE:
PLAT-10.3 The restrictions below are Acra's exact wording. What “BUY-OUT” requires: Acra confirmation requested → Q-19. \[P: Prepayment Penalty Restrictions\]

| **State** | **Restriction as printed** |
|----|----|
| AK | BUY-OUT all Residential 1-4 |
| IL | 1\) BUY-OUT all Residential 1-4 if to an ENTITY OR INDIVIDUAL and loan amount is ≤\$250,000 2) BUY-OUT all Residential 1-4 if to an INDIVIDUAL and loan amount is \>\$250,000 and interest rate is \>8% |
| KS | BUY-OUT all Residential 1-4 |
| MD | BUY-OUT all loans |
| MI | BUY-OUT all Residential 1-4 |
| MN | BUY-OUT all Residential 1-4 |

| 3 Year | 5% Fixed (5% / 5% / 5%) or 3% Fixed (3% / 3% / 3%) |

condition.source:
import rules_lib


def check(ctx):
    occupancy_subtype = ctx['occupancy_subtype']
    vacant_property = ctx['vacant_property']
    property_type = ctx['property_type']
    property_state = ctx['property_state']

    missing = rules_lib.gaps(
        occupancy_subtype=occupancy_subtype,
        vacant_property=vacant_property,
        property_type=property_type,
        property_state=property_state,
    )
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    is_non_owner_occupied = rules_lib.same(occupancy_subtype, 'non-owner occupied')
    is_not_vacant = rules_lib.flag(vacant_property) is False
    is_eligible_property_type = rules_lib.same(
        property_type, 'SFR', 'Townhome', 'PUD', 'Warrantable Condo', 'Two-Units'
    )
    is_south_dakota = rules_lib.same(property_state, 'SD')
    is_us_territory = rules_lib.same(
        property_state,
        'U.S. Terr.', 'U.S. Terrs.', 'US Territory', 'US Territories',
        'Puerto Rico', 'PR', 'Guam', 'GU', 'U.S. Virgin Islands', 'USVI', 'VI',
        'American Samoa', 'AS', 'Northern Mariana Islands', 'CNMI', 'MP',
    )

    satisfied = (
        is_non_owner_occupied
        and is_not_vacant
        and is_eligible_property_type
        and not is_south_dakota
        and not is_us_territory
    )
    return satisfied, {
        'occupancy_subtype': occupancy_subtype,
        'vacant_property': vacant_property,
        'property_type': property_type,
        'property_state': property_state,
    }

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-platinum.property_eligibility_and_property_specific_conditions.properties_listed_for_sale

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Apply the stated listed-for-sale conditions when the property was listed within the defined period.
PURPOSE: Determine whether a property listed for sale in the last six months meets the listed-property conditions, while preserving the stated applicability uncertainty.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - The property has not been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date, or is treated as a listed property for the following checks.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - Acra confirms whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged.
  - The property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).
  - If the property is an investment property, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant.
  - The loan meets the applicable channel minimum DSCR: Correspondent ≥ 1.2 or Wholesale ≥ 1.0.
  - The loan has a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
  - Twenty-four (24) months of reserves are provided.
  - The loan has a fully amortizing term and is not interest only.
  - Maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
  - No subordinate financing is present.
  - Impounds are in place.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
PLAT-7.6 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

PLAT-7.7 Whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged is part of Q-13; it is restated here because the Platinum Summary does not exclude it. \[G §11.5\]

PLAT-7.8 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI — on this program the channel minimum DSCR applies, Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-3.8), and the DTI alternative is Q-14; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

proposals.reasoning: The clause defines a property listed within the six-month period as a listed property to be considered under the following checks; listed status alone is not a failure. The function reports that classification and does not encode the reviewer-only conditions or resolve the stated uncertainty about whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged. The permitted case fields do not include listing and Application Dates, so the function uses the supplied last-six-months field.

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-platinum.property_eligibility_and_property_specific_conditions.property_type_and_location_eligibility

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Classify the property and location against the stated eligibility, ineligibility, and CLTV limits.
PURPOSE: Determine whether the property's type and location meet the published requirements and identify cases the Summary does not address.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - The property type is SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, or Two-Units.
  - The property type is not Rural Properties, Condotels, Non-Warrantable Condos, or Short-Term Rentals.
  - If the property type is Warrantable Condo or Two-Units, CLTV is no more than 75.00%.
  - The property state is not SD or a U.S. Terr.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - A three- or four-unit property, manufactured home, mixed-use property, Adult Care / Assisted Living property, or PUDtel is not treated as eligible or ineligible without Acra confirmation.
  - If the property is in a declining market, the stated -5% CLTV property/borrower full profile reduction is applied.
  - The application of the declining-market reduction in combination with other caps is confirmed by Acra.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
PLAT-1.16 Under the heading “Ineligible State: Non-Owner Occupied” the Summary lists “SD, U.S. Terrs.” \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\]

PLAT-1.17 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile”. How this reduction combines with other caps: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\]

The Platinum Summary lists eligible property types and states which types are ineligible. Features it neither lists nor excludes are marked as not addressed and asked in Q-07 rather than assumed either way.

PLAT-7.1 Eligible property types: SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Two-Units. “Two-Units, Warrantable Condo, Max CLTV: 75.00%”. \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-7.2 “Rural Properties, Condotels, Non-Warrantable Condos ineligible”; “Short-Term Rentals (STR) ineligible”. \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

| **Feature** | **Status in the Platinum Summary** | **Where stated** |
|----|----|----|
| SFR, Townhome, PUD | Expressly eligible | PLAT-7.1 |
| Warrantable Condo | Expressly eligible; maximum CLTV 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 |
| Two-Units | Expressly eligible; maximum CLTV 75.00% | PLAT-7.1 |
| Rural Properties | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 |
| Condotels | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 |
| Non-Warrantable Condos | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 |
| Short-Term Rentals | Expressly ineligible | PLAT-7.2 |
| Three- and four-unit properties | Not addressed — Q-07 | — |
| Manufactured homes | Not addressed — Q-07 | — |
| Mixed use; Adult Care / Assisted Living (§10.7) | Not addressed — Q-07 | — |
| PUDtel | Not addressed — Q-07 | — |

PLAT-7.3 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile” (PLAT-1.17). \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\]

PLAT-7.4 Ineligible locations: SD, U.S. Terrs. (PLAT-1.16). \[P: Subject Property Location Requirements\]

proposals.reasoning: The CLTV cap is 75.00% for Warrantable Condos and Two-Units only. The -5% declining-market reduction and its interaction with other caps are reviewer matters, so they are not applied here. Explicitly ineligible types and the stated ineligible locations fail; types not addressed by the Summary are reported for review rather than treated as ineligible. Missing required inputs use rules_lib.unknown.
